question: Under Montana law, engaging in real estate broker or salesperson activities without a license is prohibited. Which of the following most accurately reflects the scope of MCA 37-51-301's license requirement?
choice_a: It applies only to real estate transactions that physically close within Montana
choice_b: It applies only to full-time real estate professionals, not part-time agents
choice_c: It only restricts unlicensed individuals from listing property, not from showing property
choice_d: It prohibits unlicensed individuals from acting as a broker or salesperson, whether directly, indirectly, or through advertising such services
explanation: MCA 37-51-301 bars unlicensed persons from engaging in real estate broker or salesperson activity directly or indirectly, or from advertising such services. The requirement is not limited to where a transaction physically closes (B), does not exempt part-time agents (C), and is not narrowed to only the listing function while permitting unlicensed showings (D).

question: A Montana real estate salesperson wants to begin supervising other salespersons on behalf of a brokerage. What must that individual hold, per MCA 37-51-301?
choice_a: A valid and active Montana broker's license plus a supervising broker endorsement
choice_b: A valid salesperson's license with at least two years of experience
choice_c: Board approval alone, without any additional license or endorsement
choice_d: A broker's license from any state, regardless of Montana endorsement
explanation: MCA 37-51-301 requires anyone supervising licensed salespersons to hold a valid and active Montana broker's license and a supervising broker endorsement. Years of experience as a salesperson (A) does not substitute for a broker's license, and an out-of-state broker license without a Montana supervising broker endorsement (D) does not satisfy the statute.

question: A real estate brokerage in Montana is organized as a corporation. Under MCA 37-51-301, how must the corporation's licensing status be handled?
choice_a: The corporation itself may hold the real estate license directly
choice_b: Every corporate officer or partner who performs licensee functions must individually hold a real estate license
choice_c: Only the corporation's designated supervising broker needs a license; other officers are exempt
choice_d: Corporations are exempt from Montana's real estate licensing chapter entirely
explanation: Corporations and partnerships cannot themselves be licensed under MCA 37-51-301; instead, every corporate officer or partner performing licensee functions must individually be licensed. The entity cannot hold the license directly (A), and there is no blanket exemption for corporations (D).

question: A real estate licensee based in another state negotiates the sale of Montana real property and solicits Montana residents entirely from outside the state. Under MCA 37-51-301, is a Montana license required?
choice_a: No, because the licensee never physically enters Montana
choice_b: No, only agents physically located in Montana must be licensed for Montana transactions
choice_c: Yes, because the statute reaches activity conducted outside Montana when it involves Montana real estate or solicits Montana residents
choice_d: Only if the closing occurs through a title company physically located in Montana
explanation: MCA 37-51-301's license requirement extends to conduct occurring outside Montana when it involves Montana real property or solicitation of Montana residents, so physical presence in the state is not the deciding factor, contrary to A and B; the location of the closing title company is likewise not the trigger (C).

question: A Montana supervising broker is relocating the brokerage's designated office to a new physical address. Per MCA 37-51-308, when must the broker notify the department?
choice_a: Within 30 days after the move, with no earlier notice permitted
choice_b: Only at the broker's next annual license renewal
choice_c: There is no notice requirement as long as the current license is displayed at the old address
choice_d: Before the move, or within 10 days after the move
explanation: MCA 37-51-308 requires the broker to notify the department before removal or within 10 days after removal, along with the new address and any required fee. Waiting until the next renewal (C) or relying on the old license display (D) does not satisfy this timing requirement, and the statute does not impose a 30-day-only window (B).
source_note: MCA 37-51-308 (Broker's office -- notice to department of change of address)

question: After a Montana broker notifies the department of an office relocation and pays the required fee, what does MCA 37-51-308 provide will happen?
choice_a: The department issues a new license reflecting the new address, covering the remainder of the unexpired license period
choice_b: The department issues a brand-new license with a fresh full license term
choice_c: The broker must retake the licensing examination before a new license can issue
choice_d: The old license remains valid indefinitely and no reissued license is needed
explanation: Under MCA 37-51-308, once the department receives the change-of-address notice and fee, it issues a new license for the new location covering the unexpired portion of the current term -- not a brand-new full term (A) -- and no re-examination is required (C).
source_note: MCA 37-51-308 (Broker's office -- notice to department of change of address)

question: A Montana salesperson decides to leave their current supervising broker and join a new one. Per MCA 37-51-309, what must happen before the salesperson may begin working with the new broker?
choice_a: The salesperson may begin work immediately upon giving verbal notice to the former broker
choice_b: The salesperson must notify the department in writing, the new broker must accept in writing, and the department must issue the salesperson a new license before work begins
choice_c: Only the new supervising broker must notify the department; the salesperson need not act
choice_d: The salesperson may work under the new broker for up to 30 days while paperwork is pending
explanation: MCA 37-51-309 requires the salesperson to notify the department promptly in writing and pay the required fee, the new supervising broker to notify the department in writing of acceptance, and the department to then issue a new license and endorsement -- the salesperson may not work with the new broker until that new license issues. Verbal notice (A), broker-only action (B), and a 30-day grace period to work without the new license (D) are not what the statute provides.
source_note: MCA 37-51-309 (Change of association between broker and salesperson)

question: A Montana salesperson leaves their supervising broker, and no new supervising broker has yet accepted them. Per MCA 37-51-309, what happens to the salesperson's license?
choice_a: It remains active for up to 90 days while the salesperson searches for a new broker
choice_b: It is automatically revoked, requiring the salesperson to reapply as a new applicant
choice_c: It automatically becomes inactive, with no fee required for that status change, and the salesperson may not practice while inactive
choice_d: It stays active as long as the salesperson's continuing education is current
explanation: MCA 37-51-309 provides that if a salesperson leaves a supervising broker without a successor broker's acceptance on file, the license automatically becomes inactive with no fee, and the salesperson cannot practice during that period. It is not a 90-day active grace period (A), not a revocation requiring reapplication (B), and current continuing education does not keep it active without an accepting broker (C).
source_note: MCA 37-51-309 (Change of association between broker and salesperson)

question: Montana real estate broker and salesperson licenses issued by the Board of Realty Regulation must be renewed annually. Absent renewal, when do these licenses expire?
choice_b: On the licensee's individual birth date
choice_c: Two years from the date of initial issuance
explanation: The Board of Realty Regulation sets a uniform annual expiration of October 31, with a renewal window opening roughly 60 days beforehand. Montana does not use a birth-date renewal cycle (C) or a biennial term (D), and licenses do not run on a calendar-year December 31 expiration (B).
source_note: Montana Board of Realty Regulation, License Renewal Process (boards.bsd.dli.mt.gov/realty-regulation/license-information/renewal-process)

question: To renew an active Montana real estate license, a licensee must complete continuing education each licensing year. How many hours of continuing education does the Board require?
explanation: Active Montana real estate licensees must complete a minimum of 12 hours of continuing education each licensing year (November 1 through October 31) to renew an active license. 4 hours (D) is the supervising-broker-specific subset, not the total requirement, and 8 hours (A) is the separate one-time pre-endorsement course length for a supervising broker endorsement.
source_note: Montana Board of Realty Regulation, Continuing Education (boards.bsd.dli.mt.gov/realty-regulation/continuing-education); ARM 24.210.667

question: A Montana broker holding a supervising broker endorsement must meet the standard continuing education requirement each licensing year. Of the required hours, how many must be devoted specifically to supervising-broker topics?
choice_c: None; supervising brokers are exempt from any topic-specific requirement
explanation: A supervising broker's 12-hour annual continuing education requirement must include 4 hours specifically on supervising-broker topics -- not all of the hours (A), and supervising brokers are not exempt from a topic-specific carve-out (B). The 8-hour figure (D) is the separate one-time pre-endorsement course, not part of the annual renewal requirement.
source_note: Montana Board of Realty Regulation, Continuing Education (boards.bsd.dli.mt.gov/realty-regulation/continuing-education); ARM 24.210.667

question: A Montana real estate licensee elects to renew into inactive status rather than active status. Compared to the active renewal fee, what does the inactive renewal fee do?
choice_a: It matches the active renewal fee exactly
choice_b: It is waived entirely for inactive status
choice_c: It is reduced -- $45 for inactive renewal versus $90 for active renewal
choice_d: It permanently bars the licensee from ever reactivating
explanation: The Board sets a lower renewal fee for inactive status ($45) compared to active status ($90); the fee is not identical to active (A) and is not waived entirely (B). Renewing inactive does not permanently bar future reactivation (C) -- it simply changes the licensee's practice status and applicable continuing education/reactivation steps.
source_note: Montana Board of Realty Regulation, Real Estate Broker license page (boards.bsd.dli.mt.gov/realty-regulation/license-information/real-estate-broker)
